rhea (docs): Heads up, opened a PR to fix the /webhooks/register API ref. Current examples show a top-level `callback_url` string and a `secret` body field, but runtime expects a `callback` object with `url` and `events: []`, and returns the signing secret in the response header `x-webhook-signing-secret`. Also the OpenAPI example doesn't list allowed event enums. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4012

ishaan (eng-api): Confirmed. Runtime schema: `callback: { url: string, events: string[] }`. Valid events: `message.created`, `model.finished`, `deployment.health`. OpenAPI mistakenly documents `event` as a single string. Note: the runtime enforces HTTPS for callback URLs unless org has `allow_http_callbacks` flag; localhost is blocked by default. Also runtime returns 201 + `Location` for created webhook, and the signing secret is returned as header `x-webhook-signing-secret` not in the JSON body.

gwen (sdk): Thanks. Our JS/py snippets currently call `client.webhooks.register({ callback_url, secret })`. I'll update SDK to accept the object shape and map legacy `callback_url`/`secret` to `callback` + attach a deprecation warning. Proposed node snippet for docs to show preferred shape:
```js
await client.webhooks.create({
  callback: { url: 'https://hooks.example.com/wri', events: ['message.created', 'model.finished'] }
});
```
Also recommend adding a short migration example showing the old vs new request. I'll link the SDK PR from the docs once it's up.

omar (sec): Security notes to include in the doc: 1) treat `x-webhook-signing-secret` like a credential and store in secrets manager, do not log; 2) verification algorithm is HMAC-SHA256 over `timestamp + '.' + body` using the signing secret. Docs should show verifying headers `x-wri-timestamp` and `x-wri-signature` and include a minimal verification snippet. Example (python):
```python
import hmac, hashlib
sig = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{timestamp}.{body}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
assert hmac.compare_digest(sig, received_sig)
```
And note: rotate secrets via `DELETE /webhooks/{id}/secret` then `POST /webhooks/{id}/secret` (include sample curl).

Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4012
